headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem/clipboard/MCP plus broad egress and auto-execute-capable coding actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest external content via MCP and direct function calls, while Windsurf can read workspace files and clipboard content. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled text from aci outputs or shared files can be treated as instructions by Windsurf. The pathway is not proven by docs, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF aci writes untrusted content into a shared workspace file that Windsurf opens
IF Windsurf parses clipboard or file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Add a provenance banner to any file passed from aci to Windsurf
Require manual review before Windsurf executes instructions from shared files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or provenance tracking in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; Windsurf reads workspace files and also has broad egress plus MCP access. If sensitive aci outputs land in shared files or prompts, Windsurf can transmit them onward. The pair therefore has a realistic exfiltration path in default workflows, with no documented isolation between them.
conditions: IF aci places CRM, email, or support data into a shared workspace file
IF Windsurf forwards that file content to its model proxy or an MCP server
mitigations: Keep sensitive aci outputs out of shared folders
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
Turn off auto-sync for any workspace containing CRM or email data
Restrict Windsurf MCP servers to non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or redaction before any cross-agent transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while Windsurf supports multiple instances, writes the filesystem, and shares state via the local filesystem. Both can modify overlapping workspace artifacts, and Windsurf can also modify git state. Without locking or coordination primitives in either profile, concurrent writes can corrupt files or commits in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace directory
IF Windsurf auto-executes edits while aci is also updating shared artifacts
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent before the other edits the repo
Use git branches per agent and merge manually
Avoid simultaneous runs on the same project
requires-engineering: add file locks or an orchestrator-level mutex

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Windsurf can execute shell commands or modify git state, so one agent's output can become the other's action input. Because Windsurf has approval-per-command by default but can auto-execute, a mistaken or malicious aci output can cascade into irreversible code or operational changes. The interaction is plausible and dangerous in default workflows.
conditions: IF aci produces instructions or facts that Windsurf treats as authoritative
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled or command approval is bypassed
mitigations: Require human review of aci outputs before any Windsurf action
Keep Windsurf auto-execute disabled
Limit aci to read-only tasks when paired with Windsurf
Log and diff every command derived from aci output
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, calendar, and support data, while Windsurf handles open files and workspace files with broad network egress. If regulated customer or employee data is placed into Windsurf's workspace, it can leave the controlled environment through model proxy or MCP paths. The profiles do not show residency, retention, or DPA safeguards, so compliance risk is material.
conditions: IF regulated customer, employee, or support data is copied from aci into Windsurf workspace files
IF Windsurf sends those files to a third-party model proxy or MCP server
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf workspaces
Use a DPA-approved environment for both agents
Redact personal data before cross-agent transfer
Restrict logs and retention on shared projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for the pair
